title: Wire Transfer Finality — Core Overview (Edition 1)
description: Once a wire settles, it is effectively irreversible, unlike ACH, which can be returned within set windows. That finality makes wires a favorite target for fraud, so verification callbacks are standard practice. This overview edition presents Wire Transfer Finality as a core payments concept in modern banking.

spec.how_it_works: Instructions travel a payment rail, clear through network windows, and settle finally into the receiver's account.
spec.real_world_use: United States: Title companies verify wiring instructions by phone before closings.
spec.risk_notes: Standard controls apply: verification, monitoring, reconciliation, and documented compliance procedures.
spec.typical_costs: Costs vary by institution and usage; compare published fee schedules and compute effective cost under realistic volumes.
spec.source_note: Core facts verified from public sources.
